- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods (negative sentiment < -0.3) — model is overly conservative, often missing upward momentum.
- Lag in price recovery: model delays turning upward after a dip, especially when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.1 to -0.3).
- Overshoot after sharp spikes: model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, leading to overcorrection downward in the following days.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect toward historical mean after strong deviations, ignoring recent momentum.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bearish — adjust downward by 1–2% for early horizon.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.1, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment < -0.3, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture hidden momentum.
